final_task_tree.title: Figure out a training plan for my dog
final_task_tree.description:
Rescue border collie mix, 14 months. Pulls hard on the leash and barks at every other dog on walks. South Bay, California; I can do evenings and weekends.

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

subtasks.title: Decide: DIY training vs. hiring a pro for leash pulling + dog reactivity
subtasks.description: Question 1 of the brief. Determine whether a 14-month rescue border collie mix with hard leash pulling and barking/lunging at other dogs on walks is a DIY case or a hire-a-professional case. Look specifically at whether reactivity (barking at every dog) changes the answer vs. plain pulling. Output: a clear recommendation with the reasoning, written into this description.

subtasks.title: Find South Bay trainers who handle leash reactivity, with real prices
subtasks.description: Question 2 of the brief. Find 2-3 professionals serving the South Bay (San Jose / Sunnyvale / Santa Clara / Mountain View / Campbell area) who work on leash reactivity and leash skills with positive-reinforcement methods. Must capture actual dollar prices, format (private / group / board), and whether they have evening or weekend availability. Owner is only free evenings and weekends.

subtasks.title: Option A — Humane Society Silicon Valley "Top Dogs" reactive dog series
subtasks.description:
CONFIRMED PRICES (fetched from hssv.org, page modified Feb 2026).

Org: Humane Society Silicon Valley, 901 Ames Ave, Milpitas CA. Contact: dogtraining@hssv.org

TOP DOGS LEVEL 1 (Reactive Dogs) — $300 general registration.
- Built specifically for dogs struggling with leash or barrier reactivity.
- Format: ALL ONLINE via Zoom, for safety/control. Six-week course, one session/week. First session 90 min, then 5 sessions of 50 min.
- Eligibility: dogs 8 months and older (our dog is 14 mo = eligible); no prior bite history on dogs or people. For dogs who bark, lunge, or worry but have NOT caused injury.
- Curriculum: science-based positive reinforcement — threshold work, impulse control, calm exits, real-life coping skills.
- Next listed start: 08/19/26 at 6:15pm — an EVENING slot, fits the owner's availability.

TOP DOGS LEVEL 2 — $300. IN-PERSON, six weeks, one 50-min session/week. Prerequisite: Level 1 or instructor approval. Real-time coaching in a controlled group setting; impulse control, threshold management, coping skills, emergency exits. For reactivity only — does not address aggression.

TOP DOGS LEVEL 3 — $300. Six weeks, 50 min/week in person. Prereq L1+L2. Topic-based (rally obedience, urban agility/parkour, tricks) that continues counterconditioning around other dogs while building a sport skill.

WHY THIS FITS: cheapest credible reactivity-specific option, correct method, evening schedule, and a defined progression L1 (online, safe) -> L2 (in person around real dogs) -> L3. Note: Level 1 being online means no live practice around other dogs until Level 2.

If the dog had a bite history, HSSV asks you to email dogtraining@hssv.org for evaluation first.

subtasks.title: Option B — Orion Dog Training (San Jose) reactive dog class
subtasks.description:
CONFIRMED PRICES (fetched from oriondogtraining.com).

Org: Orion Dog Training, 576 E Santa Clara Street, San Jose (own parking lot).
Phone: 650-996-6708 (text preferred). Email: oriondogtraining@gmail.com
They offer a FREE 20-minute phone consult — start there.

"MY DOG IS REACTIVE, NOW WHAT?" — $395
- Six-week, science-based class for dogs who struggle with reactivity.
- IN PERSON, small group: 4-5 teams in a 3,000 sq ft indoor space. Whole family welcome. Homework included with video explanations.
- Schedule of the cohort found: Saturdays 5:30pm — fits weekend availability.
- *** STATUS: the Aug 1 cohort is listed FULLY BOOKED and has already started. Must call/text to ask when the next cohort opens and to get on the waitlist. ***
- Skills covered: differential marker words, emergency U-turn, reliable recall, Up & Down game, management, settle skills, Look At That (LAT) game, Catch 1-2-3 game, long-line walking and leash handling, safety gear, why dogs react.

RELATED CLASS — "CU: Pattern Games for the Distracted Dog" — $295
- Control Unleashed pattern games (Leslie McDevitt method); listed start Wednesday Aug 5 @ 7:45pm (evening).
- Good adjunct or fallback if the reactive class is full — pattern games are a core reactivity tool.

CANCELLATION POLICY: full refund within 24 hrs of booking; full refund minus 10% surcharge if more than 72 hrs before class start; no refund inside 72 hrs. No make-up classes.

WHY THIS FITS: in-person practice around other reactive dogs in a controlled indoor space, which is the thing HSSV Level 1 (online) can't give you. Curriculum is exactly the right toolkit (LAT, U-turns, pattern games).

subtasks.title: Option C — D For Dogz (Palo Alto / South Bay) Leash Reactive Dog Foundations
subtasks.description:
CONFIRMED PRICES (fetched from dfordogtraining.com).

Org: D For Dogz — trainer KT / Kaajal Tiwary. Serves Palo Alto, San Jose and the South Bay; says it has worked with 500+ Silicon Valley families. Force-free / positive reinforcement.
Phone: 650-538-3011. Free 15-minute discovery call with KT (booking widget on their site).

LEASH REACTIVE DOG FOUNDATIONS ("Growly Dog") — $595 tuition
- 9 sessions to be completed in 5 weeks.
- In-person classroom sessions: SATURDAYS 9:30-10:30 AM.
- Live Zoom Q&A / troubleshooting: WEDNESDAYS 6:30-7:15 PM (evening).
- Structure worth noting: the FIRST TWO in-person sessions are PEOPLE-ONLY, so you learn concepts and handling skills before any pressure is put on the dog. The FINAL session is a guided neighborhood walk to transition the skills to the real world.
- Content: desensitisation/counterconditioning to previously stressful stimuli, engagement games, guidance for managing reactivity outside class, owner community.

FOLLOW-ON: "Leash Reactive Dogs — About Town" membership — $500 per month
- In-person group sessions in real-world public settings, 1st and 3rd Saturdays 10:00-10:50 AM.
- Live Zoom skill-building 2nd and 4th Wednesdays.
- Includes one 60-min in-person private session OR two 30-min virtual private sessions per month, plus community access and an optional bi-weekly reactive dog support group.
- Expensive as an ongoing commitment — treat as optional, not part of the first four weeks.

FREE RESOURCE (no purchase, not a client): D For Dogz runs monthly Leash Reactive Dog Support Groups, free and open to ALL reactive dog owners in Silicon Valley. Topic-based with open Q&A, live (not recorded). Registration via their site. Worth joining regardless of which trainer you pick.

WHY THIS FITS: the people-only first sessions and the guided real-world walk at the end are the best-designed structure of the three. Most expensive of the three group options at $595.

subtasks.title: Write the week-by-week plan for weeks 1-4
subtasks.description: Question 3 of the brief. Build a concrete 4-week plan the owner can start this week, working evenings and weekends only. Must cover both problems: loose-leash walking and reactivity to other dogs. Each week needs specific drills, session lengths, and a way to tell whether it's working.
